title: Keep a failed render from landing done
lead: `slicer done S86 --render` printed `saved, but render failed` and the slice was already done. The project row template did not match the roadmap header, so the status change was written and the roadmap was left stale.
**Not in this slice:** changing which template errors render reports. The failure should still name the template problem.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `done --render` is the last step of the agent loop. If render fails, the slice should still be started, so the agent can fix the template and finish once.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- the `done` path in `src/slicer/ops.py` and the render-after-save path in `src/slicer/cli.py`
- a test that forces render to fail

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `done ID --render` against a row template that cannot render leaves the slice in its previous status and does not write the index.
2. `done ID --render` with a working template still marks the slice done and renders.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Publish the status change only after render succeeds, or roll it back when render fails. Keep the error that tells the user what to fix.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing-template case does not move the slice to done. The successful case still does.
